full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda, J:- The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order No.3 dated 20.01.2011 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Gopalgonj in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.53 of 2011 upholding the order dated 12.01.2011 passed by the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate-2, Cognizance Court No.4 (Kashiani Police Station), Gopalgonj in G.R. No.152 of 2010 arising out of Kashiani Police Station Case No.11 dated 28.12.2010 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. The informant filed an application in the Court of learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, Gopalgonj for giving the victim to his jimma and on the other hand another application was filed on behalf of victim for releasing her on her own Jimma or to the Jimma of a lawyer. The learned Senior Judicial Magistrate-2, Cognizance Court No.4, Gopalgonj observed in his order dated 12.01.2011 that it appears from the birth certificate and registration certificate the date of birth of the victim is 01.01.1995 that means she is below 16 years and is a minor. The C.S.I. for the prosecution opposed the prayers for custody of the said victim and prayed for sending her to the judicial custody. 

 7. Thereafter, the Informant being petitioner preferred the instant Revisional Application before this Court and obtained Rule and ad interim order. 

 8. The learned Sessions Judge, Gopalgonj on receiving further application on behalf of the victim girl initiated Miscellaneous Case No.86 of 2001 (without quoting any provision of Law) and on perusal of Medical Report being available in lower Court's Record, released the victim girl in the Jimma of her Lawyer, who is a interested party, as being engaged by accused persons although it appears from the order sheet dated 15.02.2011 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Gopalgonj that he received Lawyer's Certificate containing the information that the instant Criminal Revision was awaiting for order in this Court. 

 9. Thereafter the informant filed another application by Supplementary Affidavit before this Court stating that while the matter was sub-judice before this Court, the learned Sessions Judge, Gopalgonj allowed the victim girl to go in the Jimma of her lawyer and thus we are inclined to direct the learned Sessions Judge to restore the victim girl to the judicial custody as she was before passing the aforesaid order dated 15.02.2011. This direction was passed by our order dated 02.03.2011 and incompliance of the said order the victim girl was restored to the judicial custody and she was sent to the custody of Bangladesh Mahila Jatiya Ainjibi Samity, Agargaon, Dhaka. 

 10. Further development has been noticed that during the pendency of the instant Rule the Investigating Officer of the case submitted Final Report in the instant case and before acceptance by the concerned Court certified copy was supplied to the accused party. Dr. A.K.M. Akhtarul Kabir, the learned Advocate for the victim girl produced those certified copies along with the photocopies of relevant papers and documents of the records of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gopalgonj before this Court, which were kept in record and ordered to be the part of the record. 

 12. During the pendency of the hearing of the Rule we have called a report from Civil Surgeon, Gopalgonj as to whether there is any Specialist Radiological in Gopalgonj Sadar Hospital, Gopalgonj or as to whether Doctor Asit Kumar Mallick, who issued Certificate as Radiologist, certifying the age of the victim girl to be 17½  to 18½ years, is a qualified Radiologist or not. In reply to the query, Civil Surgeon, Gopalgonj by his office Memo No. স্মারক নং-সিএস/গোপা/২০১১/২২৯৫ তারিখ ৩১.৩.২০১১ informed this Court that Doctor Asit Kumar Mallick is not a Specialist in Radiology. He was absorbed against the vacant post of the Radiologist by the Director (Health), Dhaka Division, Dhaka. He further mentioned that Doctor Asit Kumar Mallick took training in Sir Salimullah Medical College and Mitford Hospital, Dhaka on Radiology for 2 months but he has no higher degree in the Radiology. Along with the aforesaid report the Civil Surgeon, Gopalgonj enclosed the certificate being issued by Sir Salimullah Medical College and Midford Hospital, Dhaka to Doctor Asit Kumar Mallick, wherein it appears that he completed training in radiology from 01.03.1999 to 30.04.1999. It is not a recognized medical degree at all. 

 13. During the hearing of the Rule the statement of the victim girl was taken in presence of the Judges of this Court by the learned Assistant Attorney General where she stated that she was examined by a Lady Doctor. On interrogation by the learned Assistant Attorney General she told, 

 14. But it is surprising to us that no Lady Doctor has put her signature in medical certificate issued by Doctor Asit Kumar Mallick, M.O. and Doctor Faridul Islam Chowdhury, RMO, Sadar Hospital Gopalgonj. All these facts rise to serious doubt about the proper examination of the victim girl medically. Let the statement of Mahmuda Rahman alias Pinky, recorded by the learned Assistant Attorney General in presence of both the Judges of this Court do form part of the record. 

 15. Now the whole crux of this case is that whether the victim girl is a minor or not. From the registration card (Secondary) of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education in respect of Mahmuda Rahman alias Pinky daughter of Sarder Lutfar Rahman it appears that date of birth is 01.01.1995 that is on the date of occurrence she was 15 years 11 months 17 days old. As per copy of the birth register which was filed in form of fristi in the Court below and the same has been filed by the learned Advocate for the petitioner before us and it appears that the date of birth of the victim girl is 01.01.1995. 

 17. In long series of decisions passed by our Appellate Division and High Court Division it has been held that the birth certificate and school certificate will prevail over the medical certificate. Reference may be made to the case of Abdul Gofran Chowdhury —v-Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and' others, reported in l984 BCR (HCD) 239 wherein it has been held that 

 "Reports of the Radiologist and the Professor of Forensic Medicine privately obtained by the accused are not of much importance to the Court-Age recorded in the Registration Card of the Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board cannot be treated as a scrap of paper and brushed aside-Report of the Medical Board received in this Court on the direction of this Court shows that the age of the girl appearing from the same and the age calculated on the basis of the Registration Card (Annexure-B), the divergence is not much-the girl is minor and it has been further held in the reported case that the opinion of the minor girl has no value in the eye of law." 

 "Statement of a victim girl in custody of the accused. It is a common knowledge that when a young girl lives with the accused after abduction she is generally prone to undue influence which is brought to bear upon her by the accused aiming at encountering the case of the lawful guardian. The statement of the victim girl under such circumstances should therefore  be taken with reservations. The Court should give more importance to the wards the parents to those of a wayward daughter who is currently enamoured, with romanticism, in deciding her custody. But in the Peculiar circumstances of the case the Appellate Division refused to interfere with the factum of her custody." 

 "Custody of the minor girl who is a victim of an offence of abduction and the opinion of a minor girl High Court Division disposed of with the direction that, "Hence it is ordered that  the victim girl is willing to go with her father, she may be allowed to go with her father, But if she does not want to go with her father then she will be kept in judicial custody till the disposal of the Criminal case as well as till she attains majority that is the age of 18 years." 

 22. We have considered the provisions of law and the facts of the case and on giving our anxious thought to the prevailing circumstances of our society, we have seen the victim girl in open Court and also in the official Chamber of the presiding Judge and we cannot but hold that she is not more than 16 years of age. Our opinion has been corroborated by the registration card and birth certificate. It is well settled principle of law that this birth certificate and school certificate will prevail over the medical certificate. Moreover, in this case from the very beginning a highhandedness has been marked by us all through that is in whole process from investigation to submission of final report. We also reiterate that final report has intentionally submitted by the Investigating Officer for favouring accused persons and to frustrate the proceeding before this Court as the matter was sub-judice before the High Court Division and it is a contemptuous act of the Police Officer, who cannot be spared at any cost. 

 23. We are sorry to observe in the judgment that the learned Sessions Judge, Gopalgonj,  ex officio, Judge of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Gopalgonj acted illegally in giving the victim girl in jimma of her lawyer, when the matter was sub-judice before the High Court Division and. moreover, the same was brought to his notice. All the above acts indicate that an unseen influential hand has played a vital role in doing all these misdeeds, even before acceptance of police report (final report), certified copies of the Police Report has been supplied and photocopies of the official records have also been supplied to the accused party. 

 25. We have heard the learned Deputy Attorney General. He submits that he cannot go beyond the decisions passed by the Appellate Division, as well this Court. 

 27. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, the impugned judgment and order No.3 dated 20.01.2011 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Gopalgonj in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.53 of 2011 upholding the order dated 12.01.2011 passed by the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate-2, Cognizance Court No.4 (Kashiani Police Station), Gopalgonj in G.R. No.152 of 2010 arising out of Kashiani Police Station Case No.11 dated 28.12.2010 is hereby set aside. The application filed by the Informant-Petitioner to hand over his victim girl Mahmuda Rahman alias Pinky to his custody is allowed. Let the victim girl Mahmuda Rahman alias Pinky be released to the custody of her father, the petitioner forthwith. The President of Bangladesh Jatiya Mahila Ainjibi Samity is directed to hand over the victim girl to her father, the petitioner before us, if she agrees to go with him, on taking proper Jimmanama. If she does not willfully go with her father she shall be sent to the judicial custody at Gopalgonj District Jail preferably with the help of Mahila Police.
